rules.title: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance - annual rent increase cap
rules.requirement: Landlords may raise rent only once a year by no more than the lesser of 3% or 80% of the CPI change. For September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027 the maximum allowable increase is 2.87%.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The increase cannot be more than 3% of your current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change, whichever is less.
rules.effective_date_note: Original ordinance effective date not stated in the document; only the current cap period (2026-09-01 to 2027-08-31) is given.

unverifiable_exemptions: exemptions under the ordinance not stated in the document

rules.title: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance - just cause and relocation
rules.requirement: A landlord must have a valid reason to evict, such as nonpayment, lease violation, or owner move-in. For certain evictions the landlord may have to help pay moving costs.
rules.key_value: just cause required; relocation assistance for certain no-fault evictions
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Your landlord must have a valid reason to evict you. This could be for not paying rent, breaking the lease, or if the landlord wants to move into the property themselves.

unverifiable_exemptions: exemptions under the ordinance not stated in the document

parsed.doc_summary: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization Office page: the rent cap is the lesser of 3% or 80% of CPI, currently 2.87% for 9/1/2026-8/31/2027. It also describes just-cause eviction with relocation assistance, a $50 registration-fee pass-through, and tenant petitions. It states no effective dates or ordinance number.
